preamble: In the Zan branch of Kartvelian (Mingrelian and Laz), Proto-Kartvelian *r became the voiced postalveolar affricate ǯ [d͡ʒ] between a vowel and a following *i, most often the nominative singular ending of consonant stems, while Georgian and Svan kept r. The correspondence Georgian -ri : Zan -ǯi is regular in inherited nouns such as 'cow', 'pig', 'ear' and 'insect, fly'. Where *r was not followed by *i it stayed r, so Mingrelian has ʕuǯ- 'ear' (< *q̇ur-i) beside ʕura 'deaf' (< *q̇ura). The change combines palatalization before a front vowel with affrication. No parallel outside Kartvelian has been found.

examples.note: The vowel also shows the Zan umlaut *o > e.
Contrast ʕura 'deaf' < *q̇ura, where no *i followed and r was kept (Thorsø 2023, §3.1.0.3).
The Laz Latin letter c stands for [d͡ʒ]; Ghvant puji has the fricative ž [ʒ] instead.
Vizha dialect; a variant ğeji has the fricative ž [ʒ].
Megrelian has č̣anǯ- with an inserted n (Thorsø 2023, §3.1.0.4).

sources: Thorsø, R. (2023). Prehistoric loanwords in Armenian: Hurro-Urartian, Kartvelian, and the unclassified substrate. PhD dissertation, Leiden University, §3.1.0.3 'R-affrication'. https://hdl.handle.net/1887/3656151
